title: Multiboot header (bootloader protocol)
summary: The Multiboot specification defines a header that bootloaders (GRUB, etc.) look for in the first 8KB of a kernel image. Header: magic (0x1BADB002), flags (32 bits), checksum (32 bits, magic + flags + checksum = 0). Optional fields depending on flags: header_addr, load_addr, load_end_addr, bss_end_addr, entry_addr. Multiboot2 uses magic 0xE85250D6.

structure.meaning: Bit 0: page align, bit 1: memory info, bit 2: video mode, bit 16: address fields present.
Physical address of the multiboot header (if flags bit 16 set).
Physical address to load the kernel.
End of BSS (uninitialized data). Kernel zeros this region.
Entry point of the kernel (EIP to jump to).

notes: Multiboot is used by GRUB, QEMU, and many bootloaders.
Multiboot 2 (magic 0xE85250D6) supports 64-bit kernels, UEFI, and more features.
The bootloader passes a multiboot info structure to the kernel (memory map, modules, etc.).
Multiboot is the standard for hobbyist OS development.
